meta.title: CZ-6A Launch visibility
notes: Forecast, not a reconstruction of this flight. NOTAM A6107/26 (issued 2026-11-20) has the same four vertices as A5283/26, the Yaogan-50 03 booster zone, so the Yaogan-50 03 revision-3 Earth-fixed ascent is reused unchanged. Yaogan-50 01, 02 and 03 each reached the RAAN that this ascent predicts for their liftoff times, to within about 0.15°.

T0 is not announced. The three earlier flights on this corridor lifted off 10, 8 and 8 min after their NOTAM opened; 13:01 UTC is the 12:53 opening plus 8 min. A T0 shift keeps the Earth-fixed track and rotates the orbit plane by 0.2507° per minute (RAAN 122.24° at 13:01).

Night launch (21:01 Beijing time): the ascent stays in Earth's shadow until T+771.9 s, at 707 km over southern Tibet, 1.5 s before stage-2 cutoff, so no twilight plume is expected. For T0 after 13:01:25 UTC no part of the powered ascent is sunlit; at the 12:53 opening sunlight arrives at T+743 s. After insertion the payload and stage stay sunlit as they head west.

Shared ascent, from the Yaogan-50 03 fit: The lower ascent is a point-mass CZ-6A with published masses and thrusts, the typical flight sequence (booster burnout 114.5 s, separation 117.5 s, fairing 179 s, stage separation 238.5 s; stage-2 ignition at 240 s is assumed), explicit drag and a fitted pitch program. One effective thrust scale was calibrated on the triangulated December 2025 CZ-6A ascent (1.06) and fitted here at 0.95. The pitch program is fitted to two untimed ground reports: at N39.00 E110.12 the rocket crossed above the Moon at 1.6x its elevation (model 1.53x), and at N37.76 E110.93 the sunlit rising path looked nearly straight. A ballistic booster range is fitted to the NOTAM booster zone (model 315 km against 350 km). The reports constrain climb geometry, not timing.

From T+300 s the stage-2 path is the revision-2 solution, fitted to the first catalog elements of 2026-240A (assumed payload; identity unconfirmed), and is kept to within 0.03 km; a bridge steering segment from ignition joins it. The cutoff state is about 3 km from that SGP4 state. The March Yaogan-50 02 reconstruction remains a weak template.

The dogleg is attributed to stage 1 and NOTAM A6107/26 to the booster drop zone. The plane change is still carried by the stage-2 steering surrogate. Staging times follow the typical published CZ-6A sequence, not this flight’s telemetry, and are not shown as timeline events.
NOTAM 12:53–13:15 UTC is a hazard-area activation interval, not launch-time limits or an insertion constraint. The 12:15–13:45 UTC selector is an exploratory range, not an announced launch window.
Shifting T0 reuses the same Earth-fixed (ECEF) trajectory and changes the solar geometry; it does not reoptimize dynamics or propagate a newly fitted orbit.

Source positions and velocities use a TEME-like frame with GMST rotation, UTC approximating UT1 and no polar motion. The exporter converts to ECEF and resamples with cubic Hermite interpolation; it does not reoptimize or integrate a new trajectory.
The upper-stage and orbit dynamics include central gravity and J2. Higher harmonics, post-insertion maneuvers, fragmentation and debris descent are not modeled.
Altitude samples are WGS84 geodetic ellipsoidal heights in km. Perigee and apogee are orbital radii minus the WGS84 equatorial radius; these are not the same altitude convention.
Sunlight uses the geometric Sun centre from the shared DE440s ephemeris and WGS84 ellipsoidal Earth occultation. The solar table is linearly interpolated in ECEF at 30-second cadence.

The 10° visibility envelope is sampled during sunlit ascent for sea-level observers with Sun-centre altitude ≤0°, then clipped to the observer night side at the insertion reference epoch. Post-insertion orbit tracks do not enlarge the ascent envelope.
No brightness, atmospheric refraction or extinction, weather, terrain, finite solar-disc emergence, or plume size is modeled. Geometric visibility is not a claim of naked-eye detection.
The 1.5 revolutions shown are exactly 1.5 times the insertion Keplerian period in elapsed time, not a claim of an exact J2 ground-track repeat or true-anomaly recurrence.

The model TLE keeps the label PRELAUNCH MODEL - NOT OBSERVED and placeholder catalog number 00000. It is fitted to the reconstructed numerical orbit and is not the catalog element set; some TLE consumers reject this placeholder.

The rocket drawing follows that sequence: the four solid boosters burn to T+114.5 s and drop at T+117.5 s, the fairing at T+179 s and stage 1 at T+238.5 s; stage 2 ignites at T+240 s, and from insertion only the payload is drawn. These are drawing states, not timeline events.
